answers.question: Is the Real ep4 drop widespread or a few images?
answers.status: official test is widespread; internal val is mixed with a repeated severe tail
answers.fact: Official test ep3 to ep4, n=100. short_ft_5ep: mean -1.240 dB, median -1.574, 79 down, 69 down by more than 1 dB, worst-10 contribution -0.397. short_ft_r2: mean -1.231, median -1.566, 78 down, 69 below -1 dB, worst-10 contribution -0.412. short_ft_w91: mean -1.542, median -1.889, 81 down, 71 below -1 dB, worst-10 contribution -0.464. Eight of the ten worst test ids are shared by all three stages: 00712, 00713, 00716, 00731, 00737, 00738, 00773, 00774. Internal val n=64: means -0.243 / -0.358 / -0.415, medians -0.165 / -0.355 / -0.316, about 33 of 64 down, 24 to 28 down by more than 1 dB. Nine val ids are in the worst 10 of every stage. Mean frac_gt1 rises from about 0.001 to 0.004-0.006. Last-10 training-batch luminance does not single out epoch 4 (Real low Y means 0.062, 0.057, 0.062 for epochs 3, 4, 5).
answers.inference: The test-set mean is not created by a handful of failures. The median drop is larger than the mean because some images improve and pull the mean up. The same images are the severe tail in every stage. Clipping of values above 1 increases, but the clipped fraction stays below 1 percent of pixels, so it is not by itself the 1.2 dB shift.
answers.missing: Whole-image light-up base and RGB residual for ep3/ep4/ep5. PNG exports are clipped and quantized and were not used as metrics.
answers.scope: Real only. Huawei and Nikon do not show this even-epoch collapse.

answers.question: Is the Nikon val/test gap a pairing or protocol error, or a set difference?
answers.status: protocol and file pairing check out; the sets differ in simple luminance; one content duplicate exists inside train/val
answers.fact: Train manifest 450, val 50, collect_triplets finds 500 Train images with a reference and 2650 without. The 500 ids equal the train+val manifest. Test has 20 images and 0 missing refs. All 20 test reference names are jpg symlinks to png files under Eval/Nikon/nanobanana_ref_Nikon. Metric protocol on the compared JSONs is rgb_float_clipped_v1, ids match across epochs, and means match per-image averages. String ids 3004 and 3016 occur in both train and test, and 3017 in both val and test, but the Low file hashes differ and the paths are Train/Low versus Test/Low. Zero realpaths are shared across splits. One Low-byte duplicate: train id 149 and val id 337, sha256 ce9c2f0cceff1db8b12315754f3f646d897096cc81ee41684ed184020789184e, different paths. Low luminance median is 0.090 train, 0.089 val, 0.168 test. Ranges overlap (train max 0.352, test min 0.033, test max 0.379). From the 100-epoch best to short_ft_r2 epoch 5: val mean delta -0.299 dB, median -0.271, 29 of 50 down; test mean +0.243, median +0.166, 15 of 20 up. Worst 5 val images contribute -0.252 of that -0.299 mean.
answers.inference: The gap is not explained by a wrong reference suffix, a missing test pair, or a different metric. The same-id strings are different files. The test lows are brighter in the center of the sample than the referenced train pool, and the test references are darker relative to GT, but the ranges overlap and n=20. The val decline and test rise are group movements in opposite directions, not one shared image.
answers.missing: Whether train 149 and val 337 also share GT and reference bytes. A larger description than global luminance. No claim of a statistically tested domain shift.
answers.scope: Does not say the internal val is useless or that test selection should be continued.
